subject: sam() producing different results depending on method of factor identification

messages.author: fdad26da462a6345
messages.subject: sam() producing different results depending on method of factor identification
parts:
Does anyone know why sam() with a latent outcome and latent predictors would be producing different results depending on whether I use the variance standardization method of factor identification (i.e., fix all latent factor variances to one with std.lv=TRUE) compared with when I use the marker method of factor identification (i.e., estimate factor variances and instead fix the first item loading of each factor to one with std.lv=FALSE)? With sem() I get the same results regardless of which method I use for identification. But with sam() I get smaller regression coefficients and a lower R2 for the dependent latent variable when I fix all latent factor variances to one.

Below is an example of my syntax; this example uses a bifactor model to measure the predictors. But I have similar issues when I model the predictor as a single factor or a correlated four-factor model. All observed indicators are polytomous.

items_IV = to("IV_",39, same_size=FALSE)
paste(items_IV,collapse="+")

items_DV = to("DV_",20, same_size=FALSE)
paste(items_DV,collapse="+")

model_bifactor <- '
#measurement model for latent predictors - bifactor model
IV_general=~IV_1+IV_2+IV_3+IV_4+IV_5+IV_6+IV_7+IV_8+IV_9+IV_10+IV_11+IV_12+IV_13+IV_14+IV_15+IV_16+IV_17+IV_18+IV_19+IV_20+IV_21+IV_22+IV_23+IV_24+IV_25+IV_26+IV_27+IV_28+IV_29+IV_30+IV_31+IV_32+IV_33+IV_34+IV_35+IV_36+IV_37+IV_38+IV_39

IV_S1=~IV_1+IV_2+IV_3+IV_4+IV_5+IV_6+IV_7+IV_8+IV_9+IV_10+IV_11
IV_S2=~IV_12+IV_13+IV_14+IV_15+IV_16+IV_17+IV_18+IV_19+IV_20+IV_21
IV_S3=~IV_22+IV_23+IV_24+IV_25+IV_26+IV_27+IV_28+IV_29+IV_30+IV_31
IV_S4=~IV_32+IV_33+IV_34+IV_35+IV_36+IV_37+IV_38+IV_39

#Restrictions to make the general and specific factors orthogonal
IV_general ~~ 0 * IV_S1
IV_general ~~ 0 * IV_S2
IV_general ~~ 0 * IV_S3
IV_general ~~ 0 * IV_S4
IV_S1 ~~ 0 * IV_S2
IV_S1 ~~ 0 * IV_S3
IV_S1 ~~ 0 * IV_S4
IV_S2 ~~ 0 * IV_S3
IV_S2 ~~ 0 * IV_S4
IV_S3 ~~  0 * IV_S4

#measurement model for dependent variable:
outcome=~DV_1+DV_2+DV_3+DV_4+DV_5+DV_6+DV_7+DV_8+DV_9+DV_10+DV_11+DV_12+DV_13+DV_14+DV_15+DV_16+DV_17+DV_18+DV_19+DV_20

#Structural model (excluding covariates)
outcome~IV_general+IV_S1+IV_S2+IV_S3+IV_S4
'



###SEM MODELS - THESE TWO SEM MODELS PRODUCE THE SAME RESULTS
fit_sem_v1=lavaan::sem(data=df, model=model_bifactor, ordered=c(items_IV,items_DV),
                                                estimator="wlsmv",
                                                std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fit_sem_v1, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

fit_sem_v2=lavaan::sem(data=df, model=model_bifactor, ordered=c(items_IV,items_DV),
                    estimator="wlsmv",
                    std.lv=FALSE)
summary(fit_sem_v2, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)


###SAM MODEL - THESE TWO SAM MODELS PRODUCE DIFFERENT RESULTS
fit_sam_v1 <- sam(model=model_bifactor, data=df, std.lv=TRUE, ordered=c(items_IV,items_DV), mm.list=list(IV=c("IV_general","IV_S1","IV_S2","IV_S3","IV_S4"), DV=c("outcome")), sam.method = "global")

summary(fit_sam_v1, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)


fit_sam_v2 <- sam(model=model_bifactor, data=df, std.lv=FALSE, ordered=c(items_IV,items_DV), mm.list=list(IV=c("IV_general","IV_S1","IV_S2","IV_S3","IV_S4"), DV=c("outcome")), sam.method = "global")

summary(fit_sam_v2, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: sam() producing different results depending on method of factor identification
parts:
Hello Hilary,

I am not sure. Would you be able to send me a reprex?

I would expect that std.lv = TRUE/FALSE give different results (for the
regression coefficients) both for sem() and sam(). Unless the factor
variances happen to be close to 1.0 even if std.lv = FALSE.

But sem() and sam() should be close to each other in that respect. At
least with some toy data, that seems to be the case. Maybe it has
something to do with the bifactor model, but I am not sure. That is why
I would like to investigate this further.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: sam() producing different results depending on method of factor identification
parts:
This turned out to be an issue with sam.method = "global" + std.lv =
TRUE in general.

Long story short: std.lv = TRUE fixes the latent (residual) variances to
1, and they are never free parameters. But in global SAM, we need to
free up the residual variances of the endogenous/dependent latent
variables in step 2, otherwise, we fix the residual variance to one
while in step 1 (measurement only), we fixed the total variance to one.

I believe this is now fixed in the github version of lavaan (0.6-20.2290)

Yves.
